derivation: Use `Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor B J`: it identifies `B ⧸ I[B]` with `(A ⧸ J) ⊗[A] B`, with quotient classes sent to `1 ⊗ₜ b`. Transport along `e` and use `he` to obtain surjectivity and the kernel inclusion.
explanation: The Mathlib algebra equivalence presents this tensor product as the quotient of `B` by the extended ideal `Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) J`, which is exactly `I[B]`. Its quotient map therefore has image all of the tensor product and kernel `I[B]`; the given algebra equivalence and compatibility hypothesis transfer those facts to `σ`. This is a specialization of the quotient–tensor equivalence, not the same stated theorem.
